provider: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (CDSE / ESA DIAS) - 12 TB/month of free READ, zero writable storage

free_tier.stated: 12 TB per rolling 30 days of download via S3/OData/STAC for a Copernicus General User, 20 MB/s per connection, 4 concurrent connections, 2,000 requests/min, empty-account registration. After the transfer limit is hit, bandwidth drops to 1 MB/s and 1 concurrent connection until the 30-day total falls back under the limit. Data Workspace adds 0.1 TB/month of deferred-access transfer and 25 processed products/month. JupyterLab gives 10 GB of persistent scratch, 30-day idle expiry.

egress.terms: The whole quota IS egress - this is the largest free read allowance found anywhere in the programme, but there is no general-purpose bucket to write to.

tooling: S3 credentials self-service from the user panel against eodata.dataspace.copernicus.eu; openEO API (10,000 credits/month, temporary boost); Sentinel Hub APIs (10,000 requests/month); s3cmd/boto3 documented.
chaining: Per account, and the 30-day rolling window means 12 TB/month sustained without cycling accounts. Creodias resells the same platform with paid extensions.
limits_note: Read-only EO products. No user-owned bucket: the S3 endpoint serves the mission archive. Registration is open to anyone with an email and is self-service.
reliability_note: CloudFerro-operated for ESA; the 1 MB/s throttle after the cap is a hard cliff, not a soft degrade.
